newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures settle higher with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures settle higher with cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Monday, continuing recent gains on stronger cash prices in the western U.S.
"It was basically the cash market," said one Houston futures trader when asked about the factor in today's rise.
Day-ahead electricity prices at the California-Oregon Border (COB) climbed 50 cents to a dollar $14.00-15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), while those at Palo Verde (PV) held steady at $17.00-18.00.

Short-term power supply in the West will tighten Tuesday when the Western Area Power Administration (WAPA) trimmed power offers from the 1,855 megawatt (MW) Salt Lake Integrated hydroelectric project.
Strength in the natural gas market also supported the electricity complex, market sources said.

Swing natural gas prices across the country on average rose three to five cents per million British thermal units (mmBtu) today on cooler weather in the East and storage buying in the domestic producing region.
NYMEX April Henry Hub gas futures settled down 1.0 cent at $1.937/mmBtu, erasing a 9.3 cent gain due to a late technical selloff.
April COB finished up 23 cents at $10.22 a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded between $10.00 and $10.35.
May COB ended up 32 cents at $10.20. Other active COB months settled 15 to 65 cents higher.
April PV finished up 30 cents at $14.40, its highest level in two months.
May PV ended also settled up 30 cents at $14.50. Other deferred PV contracts ended 20 to 40 cents higher.
In the Northwest, temperatures were expected to average near to slightly below normal for much of the week, with a chance of rain and mountain snow through Thursday.
Most of the Southwest was expected to experience well-above normal readings in the early part of this week as a high pressure system hovered over the region.
Restart of the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre nuclear unit 2 in San Clemente, Calif., was planned for March 20.
Also, Arizona Public's 1,221 megawatt Palo Verde nuclear unit 3 was expected to return to service from a scheduled maintenance and refueling shutdown in early April.
NYMEX estimated 130 COB and 204 PV contracts were sold, compared with 118 COB and 347 PV lots Friday.
